# Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Important genetic syndromes > Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome*

[Original Article Link](/library/hk0cnT)

---

## Summary

<u>Marfan syndrome</u> (MFS) is an <u>autosomal dominant</u> <u>connective tissue disorder</u> that affects the microfibrils and <u>elastin</u> in <u>connective tissue</u> throughout the body. MFS is associated with disorders of the <u>cardiovascular system</u> (e.g., <u>mitral valve prolapse</u>, <u>aortic aneurysm</u>, and dissection), the <u>musculoskeletal system</u> (e.g., <u>tall stature</u> with disproportionately long extremities, <u>joint hypermobility</u>), and the eyes (e.g., <u>subluxation of the lens</u> of the <u>eye</u>).




<u>Ehlers-Danlos syndrome</u> (<u>EDS</u>) is a heterogeneous group of <u>connective tissue disorders</u> with variable inheritance (including hypermobility <u>EDS</u> and <u>vascular EDS</u>), characterized by defective <u>collagen synthesis</u> and processing. Symptoms include varying degrees of hyperextensive <u>skin</u>, <u>joint hypermobility</u>, and tissue fragility (including that of vasculature).




The diagnosis of MFS and <u>EDS</u> is based on clinical criteria. <u>Genetic testing</u> can be used additionally to confirm or rule out the diagnosis of certain subtypes. Since there is currently no causal treatment for MFS or <u>EDS</u>, management typically involves an approach focusing on clinical features, including regular monitoring of complications (e.g., imaging of <u>aortic aneurysm</u>) and preventive care (e.g., <u>antihypertensives</u> to prevent <u>aneurysm</u> progression).

## Etiology and classification

### <u>Marfan syndrome</u> [[1]](/library/rXafzQ)[[2]](/library/IXaYzQ)




* Mutation of fibrillin-1 gene (<u>FBN1</u>);  on <u>chromosome</u> 15 → defective <u>fibrillin</u> (a glycoprotein that forms a supportive sheath around <u>elastin</u>) → defective <u>connective tissue</u> microfibrils → defective <u>elastin</u>

* Several hundred different <u>FBN1</u> mutations have been described in patients with <u>Marfan syndrome</u>.

* <u>Autosomal dominant</u>;  <u>inheritance pattern</u> with variable <u>penetrance</u>





> [!NOTE]
> MarFan syndrome is caused by a <u>gene</u> mutation in FBN1 on <u>chromosome</u> 15 (Fifteen), resulting in defective Fibrillin protein.




### <u>Ehlers-Danlos syndrome</u> [[1]](/library/rXafzQ)




* Mutations in <u>genes</u> (e.g., COL5A1, COL3A1) that control the synthesis and processing of different <u>types of collagen</u> → <u>collagen</u> defects;  (e.g., a defect in <u>lysine</u>-<u>hydroxylysine</u> cross-linking of <u>tropocollagen</u> leads to unstable <u>collagen fibrils</u>  or <u>procollagen</u> peptidase deficiency ) [[3]](/library/GxWBBn0)

* <u>Autosomal dominant</u> or recessive inheritance with varying patterns of inheritance, severity, and type of <u>collagen</u> affected

* <u>Ehlers-Danlos syndrome</u> is subclassified into 13 different types, based on clinical presentation, genetic defect, and type of <u>collagen</u> affected (e.g., hypermobility type, classical type). Only the most common types are discussed here.





| <br>Types of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (<u>EDS</u>) <br> |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | <br>Hypermobile EDS (most common) | Classic EDS | Classical-like EDS | Vascular EDS |
| Genetic defect |  | <br>* Unknown<br><br> | <br><br>* COL5A1<br><br>* COL5A2<br><br><br> | <br>* TNXB<br><br> | <br>* COL3A1<br><br> |
| Affected protein |  | <br>* <u>Type V collagen</u><br><br> | <br>* Tenascin X<br><br> | <br>* Type III <u>procollagen</u><br><br> |  |
| Distinguishing features | <u>Joints</u> | <br><br>* <u>Joint</u> instability (e.g., shoulder and patella <u>dislocations</u>) predominates<br><br>* Small and <u>large joint</u> hypermobility<br><br>* Chronic <u>joint</u> <u>pain</u><br><br>* Premature <u>osteoarthritis</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Generalized <u>joint hypermobility</u> and subluxations (e.g., patella, temporomandibular, shoulder)<br><br> | <br>* Generally milder features than in <u>classic EDS</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Small joint</u> hypermobility is less prominent than in other <u>EDS types</u><br><br> |

## Clinical features

### <u>Marfan syndrome</u> [[1]](/library/rXafzQ)[[4]](/library/xXaEZj)[[5]](/library/BXazZj)




#### Cardiovascular




Cardiac findings in Marfan syndrome include:




* Aortic disease

* Caused by aortic <u>necrosis</u> (<u>cystic medial degeneration</u>) → weakening of the <u>elastic artery</u>

* Manifestations include:

* <u>Aortic aneurysm</u>

* Thoracic or <u>abdominal aortic aneurysm</u>

* Aortic root dilation: <u>aneurysm</u> of the <u>proximal</u> <u>thoracic aorta</u>

* <u>Aortic regurgitation</u>

* <u>Aortic dissection</u> (typically of the <u>thoracic aorta</u>)

* <u>Mitral valve prolapse</u>

* <u>Berry aneurysms</u>: rupture leads to <u>subarachnoid hemorrhage</u>





#### Musculoskeletal




* <u>Tall stature</u> and long extremities

* <u>Joint hypermobility</u>  

* Positive thumb sign (Marfan disease): Patients are asked to place their thumbs in the palms of the same hand and then clench to form a fist. A positive sign is present when the thumb protrudes beyond the ulnar border of the hand.

* Positive wrist sign: Patients are asked to clasp the wrist of the opposite hand. A positive <u>wrist sign</u> is present when the little finger and thumb overlap.

* High-arched <u>palate</u>

* <u>Arachnodactyly</u>;  (achromachia): abnormally long, slender fingers and toes

* Pectus deformity

* Pectus carinatum: a sternal deformity where the middle and lower portion of the <u>sternum</u> protrude forward (also known as <u>sternal kyphosis</u>)

* Pectus excavatum: a sternal deformity where the middle and lower portion of the <u>sternum</u> protrudes inward

* <u>Pes planus</u> (<u>flat foot</u>) or hindfoot valgus

* Spinal deformities (<u>scoliosis</u>, <u>hyperkyphosis</u>)

* Vertical overdevelopment of the head (<u>dolichocephaly</u>)

* <u>Winged scapula</u>

* Habitual <u>dislocations</u> (particularly the patella and shoulder)

* <u>Acetabular</u> protrusion

#### <u>Skin</u>




* Hyperextensive <u>skin</u>

* Formation of <u>striae</u> (<u>stretch marks</u>)





#### Eyes




* Visual impairment: <u>ectopia lentis</u> (<u>lens dislocation</u>) → <u>lens subluxation</u> superiorly and temporally

* Severe <u>myopia</u>

* <u>Retinal detachment</u>

* <u>Glaucoma</u>

* Early <u>cataract</u> formation





![Lens subluxation in Marfan syndrome](media/yazb0qtcpsh529p1vj927u4i.jpg)

Lens subluxation in Marfan syndrome

![Retinal detachment in Marfan syndrome](media/cke1sdolmmsm7i6c6lh1267j.jpg)

Retinal detachment in Marfan syndrome




#### Other




* Increased risk of <u>spontaneous pneumothorax</u>

* Lumbosacral dural ectasia





> [!TIP]
> The classic presentation of MFS includes <u>aortic aneurysm</u> or dissection, long extremities, <u>arachnodactyly</u>, <u>joint hypermobility</u>, and <u>subluxation of the lens</u> of the <u>eye</u>.




### <u>Ehlers-Danlos syndrome</u> [[6]](/library/AXaR0j)




The clinical features discussed here are seen in all <u>types of EDS</u>, but their severity may vary and certain symptoms predominate depending on the specific type.




#### Cardiovascular




Cardiac findings in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome include:




* <u>Heart valve</u> defects (e.g., <u>mitral valve prolapse</u>)

* <u>Cystic medial degeneration</u>: can lead to aortic dilation, <u>aneurysms</u>, or dissection

* <u>Aneurysms</u>/dissections of the iliac, splenic, or <u>renal arteries</u>

* <u>Berry aneurysms</u>: rupture leads to <u>subarachnoid hemorrhage</u>





#### Musculoskeletal




* <u>Joint hypermobility</u> with a tendency towards <u>dislocation</u>

* Skeletal abnormalities (e.g., <u>scoliosis</u>, pectus deformity)





![Joint hypermobility](media/dsaq1pgd8i7f9y3e01gjodnm.jpg)

Joint hypermobility




#### <u>Skin</u>




* Tendency to <u>bruise</u> easily

* <u>Skin hyperextensibility</u>

* Frequent <u>skin</u> <u>lacerations</u> (e.g., with minor scratches)

* Poor <u>skin</u> healing (e.g., following <u>surgery</u> )

* <u>Atrophic</u> scars





![Facial features of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome](media/s3hj2i7srdsqvooezu4ixyg2.jpg)

Facial features of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

![Skin hyperextensibility in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome](media/ghme1hbvc024lleynsb3g6bn.jpg)

Skin hyperextensibility in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome




#### Eyes




* <u>Myopia</u>

* <u>Retinal detachment</u> and tears





#### Other




* <u>Hernias</u>

* Organ rupture (e.g., gravid <u>uterus</u>) causing <u>pain</u> and (potentially life-threatening) internal bleeding, especially seen with <u>vascular EDS</u>

* <u>Cervical insufficiency</u>, <u>uterine prolapse</u>

* Dental abnormalities: hypodontia, delayed eruption, molluscoid pseudotumors





> [!TIP]
> The classic presentation of <u>EDS</u> involves <u>hyperextensible skin</u>, <u>joint hypermobility</u>, and a tendency to bleed easily.

---

## Diagnosis

* MFS and <u>EDS</u> are typically <u>clinical diagnoses</u>.

* MFS and certain <u>types of EDS</u> can be confirmed or ruled out with <u>genetic testing</u>.

* Tests to identify specific manifestations:

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (cardiovascular manifestations)

* <u>Slit-lamp examination</u> (to rule out <u>lens</u> abnormalities)

* Imaging: skeletal <u>x-rays</u> and <u>MRI</u> (dural ectasia in <u>Marfan syndrome</u>) [[7]](/library/-t0DT3)[[8]](/library/ZF0Zg3)





![Thumb sign in Marfan syndrome](media/to5zkr9te96vvtvondw23fah.jpg)

Thumb sign in Marfan syndrome

---

## Pathology

* Cystic medial degeneration: a degeneration (<u>necrosis</u>) of <u>large blood vessels</u> such as the aorta. [[9]](/library/fUYkco)

* Seen in disorders that cause increased arterial wall <u>stress</u> (e.g., <u>hypertension</u>, <u>coarctation of the aorta</u>) as well as <u>connective tissue disorders</u> (especially MFS and <u>EDS</u>)

* Can lead to <u>aortic aneurysm</u> and <u>aortic dissection</u>

* <u>Histopathology</u> 

* Loss, thinning, disorganization, and fragmentation of elastic tissue in the media

* Accumulation of mucoid <u>extracellular matrix</u>

* Loss of <u>smooth muscle</u> <u>nuclei</u>




![Cystic medial degeneration (cystic medial necrosis)](media/sxujljc5jktxj9pft0stguok.jpg)

Cystic medial degeneration (cystic medial necrosis)

## Differential diagnoses

| Differential diagnosis of a marfanoid body habitus |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | <u>Inheritance pattern</u> | Skeletal | <u>Dermal</u> | Vascular | Other |
| <u>Marfan syndrome</u> | <br>* <u>Autosomal dominant</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Tall stature</u> (increased arm-to-height <u>ratio</u>)<br><br>* <u>Arachnodactyly</u><br><br>* <u>Joint hypermobility</u><br><br>* <u>Scoliosis</u><br><br>* Pectus deformity<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Hyperextensive <u>skin</u><br><br>* <u>Striae</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Aortic root dilation</u><br><br>* <u>Mitral valve prolapse</u><br><br>* <u>Aortic dissection</u><br><br>* <u>Berry aneurysms</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Upward <u>lens dislocation</u><br><br>* <u>Myopia</u>, <u>retinal detachment</u><br><br>* No <u>intellectual disability</u><br><br><br> |
| <u>Ehlers-Danlos syndrome</u> | <br>* <u>Autosomal dominant</u> or recessive<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Joint hypermobility</u><br><br>* <u>Scoliosis</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Hyperextensive <u>skin</u><br><br>* Easy <u>bruising</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Aortic dissection</u><br><br>* <u>Berry aneurysms</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Myopia</u>, <u>retinal detachment</u><br><br>* Organ rupture/prolapse<br><br>* Dental abnormalities<br><br><br> |
| <u>Homocystinuria</u> | <br>* <u>Autosomal recessive</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Tall stature</u><br><br>* <u>Arachnodactyly</u><br><br>* <u>Scoliosis</u><br><br>* Pectus deformity<br><br>* <u>Osteoporosis</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Light <u>skin</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Thrombosis</u><br><br>* <u>Arteriosclerosis</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Downward <u>lens dislocation</u>, <u>myopia</u><br><br>* <u>Intellectual disability</u><br><br>* <u>Megaloblastic anemia</u><br><br>* <u>Seizures</u><br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Loeys-Dietz syndrome</u> [[10]](/library/Svbyzv)<br> | <br>* <u>Autosomal dominant</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Scoliosis</u><br><br>* Pectus deformity<br><br>* <u>Cleft palate</u><br><br>* <u>Craniosynostosis</u><br><br>* <u>Osteoporosis</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Easy <u>bruising</u><br><br> | <br>* <u>Congenital heart defects</u> (e.g., <u>ASD</u>)<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Hypertelorism</u>, <u>blue sclerae</u><br><br>* Abdominal <u>pain</u>, <u>diarrhea</u><br><br>* Organ rupture<br><br><br> |
| <u>Multiple endocrine neoplasia 2B</u> (<u>MEN 2B</u>) | <br>* <u>Autosomal dominant</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Tall stature</u> (increased arm-to-height <u>ratio</u>)<br><br>* <u>Arachnodactyly</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Multiple <u>neurinomas</u> of the <u>lips</u>, <u>tongue</u>, and lining of the mouth<br><br> | <br>* Unaffected<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Pheochromocytoma</u><br><br>* <u>Medullary thyroid carcinoma</u><br><br>* Eyes are unaffected<br><br><br> |
| <br>Congenital contractural arachnodactyly (<u>Beals syndrome</u>) [[11]](/library/Rvbl-v)[[12]](/library/ivbJ-v)<br> | <br>* <u>Autosomal dominant</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Tall stature</u><br><br>* <u>Arachnodactyly</u><br><br>* <u>Joint contractures</u><br><br>* <u>Scoliosis</u><br><br>* Craniofacial abnormalities<br><br><br> | <br>* Unaffected<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Aortic root dilation</u><br><br>* <u>Mitral valve prolapse</u><br><br><br> | <br>* <u>Intestinal atresia</u>, malrotation<br><br> |





> [!TIP]
> <u>Marfan syndrome</u> classically manifests with a superior and temporal displacement of the <u>lens</u> (upward and outward). <u>Homocystinuria</u> also results in a <u>Marfanoid habitus</u> but manifests with inferior and <u>medial</u> displacement of the <u>lens</u> (downward and inward).




The differential diagnoses listed here are not exhaustive.

---

## Treatment

### Applicable to MFS and <u>EDS</u>




* No causal treatment

* Interdisciplinary treatment of specific symptoms and manifestations, including:

* Aortic dilatation: <u>beta blockers</u> and, if necessary, aortic root replacement <u>surgery</u>

* <u>Scoliosis</u>: bracing and, if necessary, <u>surgery</u>

* <u>Physical therapy</u>

* <u>Pain</u>: <u>analgesia</u>

* Regular orthopedic, ophthalmological, and cardiological check-ups





### Specific treatment [[13]](/library/aF0Qg3)




* <u>Marfan syndrome</u>

* <u>Angiotensin receptor blockers</u> (<u>ARBs</u>) can be used in combination with <u>beta blockers</u> to lower blood pressure.

* The <u>efficacy</u> of <u>ARBs</u> (e.g., <u>losartan</u>) in preventing <u>aortic root dilation</u> is subject to current research.

* <u>Ehlers-Danlos</u> syndrome: High-contact sports should be avoided and surgical procedures should be performed with caution in order to avoid excessive <u>bruising</u> and internal bleeding.

---

## Prognosis

### <u>Marfan syndrome</u> [[1]](/library/rXafzQ)[[14]](/library/zXar0j)




* Normal <u>life expectancy</u>: if diagnosed early and complications are managed appropriately

* Cardiovascular complications: Disease progression should be carefully monitored and managed accordingly to prevent cardiovascular complications (e.g., <u>aortic dissection</u>).

* Aortic root disease (e.g., <u>aneurysm</u>, dissection) is the most common <u>cause of death</u>.





### <u>Ehlers-Danlos syndrome</u> [[8]](/library/ZF0Zg3)[[15]](/library/_Xa50j)[[16]](/library/-XaD0j)




* Normal <u>life expectancy</u> in all <u>types of EDS</u> except vascular type

* <u>Life expectancy</u> in vascular type: approx. 50 years
